1. Demand-pull inflation: When the demand for goods and services exceeds the supply, prices tend to rise. This can happen when there is an increase in consumer spending, government spending, or investment.

2. Cost-push inflation: When the cost of producing goods and services increases, prices tend to rise. This can happen when there is an increase in wages, raw material prices, or energy prices.

3. Built-in inflation: This occurs when the economy is operating at a level of production that is not sustainable in the long run
